title: Mirabel and the Uniform
premise: Mirabel Joubert, a seamstress who mends uniforms in a dying republic's capital, shares a cramped household with her brother Theo, a diplomatic courier carrying the codes of a government already negotiating its own surrender. When a sealed letter meant for a dead minister is misdelivered to their door, the Jouberts learn their late father's name sits on a list of collaborators — and that whoever holds the letter can save or condemn the family's memory. As the city fractures and the last evacuation ship is readied, Mirabel must decide which of them — herself, Theo, or the orphaned ward they've raised as a sister — takes the final berth before the century turns. In the end she gives the berth away, stays behind with the letter burned and the truth kept, and builds a new kind of family from the ones the republic left ashore.
about_author: Isandro Nakamura is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the private letters of displaced families. They write historical fiction about the small, stubborn households history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Mending Room
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In the winter of a collapsing republic, Mirabel repairs officers' uniforms by lamplight while Theo returns from a courier run with frostbitten hands and a sealed satchel he won't discuss. The beat is quiet domesticity stretched over dread, establishing the family: Mirabel, Theo, and young ward Colette.

chapters.title: A Letter for a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A misdirected sealed letter arrives addressed to Minister Aubry — who died a week ago at their father's old address. Theo insists on returning it unopened; Mirabel, recognizing their father's handwriting on the enclosure, hesitates. The beat is temptation: the first crack in the family's careful invisibility.

chapters.title: Codes and Needles
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo reveals he carries diplomatic codes for a government that no longer exists on any map, and that the letter may name collaborators — their father among them. Mirabel sews a hidden pocket into his courier coat. The beat is complicity: the siblings choose to open what should have stayed shut.

chapters.title: The List
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Inside the letter: a list of names, their father's circled in ink still wet when he died. A name they don't recognize — Delorme — appears twice. Colette asks too many questions at dinner. The beat is vertigo, the past arriving with a knock instead of gradually.

chapters.title: Delorme Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A courteous stranger named Delorme visits, claiming to be an old regimental friend of their father, and asks after 'the papers.' Theo lies well for the first time in his honest life. The beat is fear wearing a friendly face, and Theo's discovery that lying is easier than he'd hoped.

chapters.title: Colette's War
chapters.summary: Colette's POV. Fifteen-year-old Colette, orphaned by the border war, has been passing intelligence she overhears in the mending room to a boy she loves. She realizes too late that one of her tidbits involved the letter. The beat is guilt and the terrible power of being underestimated.

chapters.title: What Father Buried
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Searching their father's old tailor shop, Mirabel finds a second copy of the list and a letter to her: an admission that he informed to save the family, once, long ago. The beat is grief reframed — inheritance as both wound and instruction.

chapters.title: The Evacuation Lists
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The republic announces its final evacuation; berths are assigned by name and favor. Theo's courier status could secure one seat. One. The word 'one' sits at the dinner table like a fourth guest. The beat is the theme made arithmetic: love measured in seats.

chapters.title: Delorme's Offer
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Delorme returns, no longer pretending: he offers two berths and the family's cleared name in exchange for the letter and the list. Mirabel understands he isn't a collaborator — he's a son, doing for his father what she is doing for hers. The beat is unwanted recognition.

chapters.title: Night of the Posters
chapters.summary: Colette's POV. The city erupts; occupation posters go up overnight naming collaborators, and their father's name — from a leaked fragment — appears on a wall outside the shop. A mob gathers; neighbors who took Mirabel's mending for free stand silent. The beat is betrayal by the ordinary world.

chapters.title: The Boy at the Bridge
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Colette's boy, Luc, is caught carrying her notes and detained. Theo trades a favor from his courier years to get him released, burning his last claim to official protection. The beat is sacrifice without applause — Theo spending his currency on someone else's child.

chapters.title: Three Berths, One Ship
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Delorme's deadline arrives: the letter by dawn, and the berths — now two, the offer reduced — leave at noon. Theo argues they take them and let the past burn. Mirabel argues the truth is the only inheritance worth keeping. The beat is the family's first real fracture.

chapters.title: Colette Runs
chapters.summary: Colette's POV. Believing she is the reason for everything, Colette takes the letter and goes to Delorme herself to trade it for the family's safety. The beat is a child trying to carry an adult's war, and the reader's heart in her throat as she crosses the occupied quarter alone.

chapters.title: The Exchange That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel intercepts Colette at Delorme's rooms and finds him packing to flee — his own name has surfaced on the new regime's list. He returns the letter, unfinished. The beat is the collapse of the antagonist into a mirror: two families, same arithmetic, no winners.

chapters.title: Ashes in the Mending Room
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo burns the letter and the list, arguing that names only have power on paper. Mirabel lets him — then reveals she memorized every name, including Delorme's. The beat is the siblings' reconciliation through mutual, stubborn honesty.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At the docks, the final berth is theirs: one seat, noon sailing, no extensions. Theo claims it as the courier and eldest; Colette is a minor with a legal claim; Mirabel is neither. The beat is the novel's crux — the choice made explicit, and Mirabel already knowing her answer.

chapters.title: What Mirabel Decided
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel forges Delorme's cleared name onto Colette's papers — the one dishonest act of an honest woman — and puts her sister on the ship. Theo, refusing to leave her, gives his berth to a stranger's infant at the gangplank. The beat is love outbidding duty on both sides.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. New Year's Eve in an occupied city: church bells, blacked-out windows, Mirabel and Theo sharing one coat. They reopen the tailor shop under a neutral sign. The beat is grief and relief braided together — the family smaller and larger at once.

chapters.title: Letters Without Addresses
chapters.summary: Colette's POV. From across the water, Colette writes letters she cannot send, and sends them anyway through a smuggler who reads every one. She learns the trade of survival in a new country. The beat is homesickness as a form of loyalty, and the first flicker of her own agency.

chapters.title: The Shop on Rue Verte
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Two years on: the shop thrives quietly, mending uniforms for whoever governs. Delorme's daughter appears at the counter with a coat and her father's apology in an envelope. Mirabel mends the coat and keeps the envelope unopened. The beat is mercy as a daily practice, not a gesture.

chapters.title: The Berth That Came Back
chapters.summary: Colette's POV. Colette returns at nineteen, unannounced, with papers in three names and Luc waiting in a doorway. The reunion is awkward, ordinary, real — no speeches. The beat is the found family completing its circle: everyone who was given away comes home by their own road.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Years later, Mirabel teaches Colette's daughter to sew, and tells her the family story with the dangerous names left out and the important ones left in. The final image: a uniform in the shop window, mended so well no one can see the seams. The beat is peace — inheritance as what you choose to carry forward.
